source_reference.source_text: Fannie Mae can only purchase loans up to a certain dollar amount. This dollar amount is known as the conforming loan limit. Fannie Mae’s loan limits are imposed under its federal charter as amended by law. The loan limits apply to all conventional loans delivered to Fannie Mae for whole loan purchase or MBS pool issuance and are based on the original loan amount of the loan (irrespective of the origination date). The limits are subject to change annually and vary, depending upon the number of units in the property and the property’s location. The conforming loan limits are posted on Fannie Mae's website . Lenders are responsible for ensuring that the original loan amount of each loan does not exceed the applicable maximum loan limit for the speciﬁc area in which the property is located at the time the loan is delivered to Fannie Mae.

Once the permanent loan is identified as the delivery subject, B102's applicable loan-limit test must be run for a whole-loan purchase or MBS pool issuance. business_rules.rule_name: Inspection and property-condition requirements for rural high-needs value acceptance
business_rules.description: When exercising the rural high-needs value acceptance offer, the lender must obtain and review a sufficient inspection report, retain it in the loan file, complete required repairs before delivery, obtain the borrower's inspection affidavit, confirm an inspection contingency and inspector liability insurance, and use a properly qualified professional inspector.
business_rules.inference_reasoning: The excerpt expressly states that the listed inspection requirements must be met for the lender to exercise the rural high-needs value acceptance offer.

source_reference.source_text: The lender must obtain a home inspection to determine the property condition. The inspection report must be retained in the loan ﬁle and made available to Fannie Mae upon request. review the inspection report to verify the property condition. The content of the inspection report must be suﬃcient for the lender to determine whether the property is safe, sound, and structurally secure. Any issues that compromise safety, soundness, or structural integrity must be repaired before loan delivery. obtain an aﬃdavit signed by the borrower(s) conﬁrming that they received a copy of the property inspection report, read the report, and were notiﬁed of any lender-required repairs. conﬁrm that the purchase contract contains an inspection contingency that oﬀers the borrower(s) enough time to cancel the contract without penalty if they so choose, should the inspection reveal an issue with the property. conﬁrm that the inspector has liability insurance. use a professional inspector that meets the state license and education requirements for those states that regulate inspectors.

dependencies.rationale: The value acceptance eligibility rule identifies the transaction and property conditions under which the rural high-needs offer may be used. Once that offer is exercised, the inspection rule imposes mandatory inspection, affidavit, insurance, qualification, repair, and retention requirements.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If the source eligibility determination is not completed or the offer is not properly exercised, the system cannot determine whether the special inspection obligations apply. If the offer is exercised without satisfying the inspection rule, the lender may be unable to deliver the loan, may lack required loan-file documentation, and may expose the property to unresolved safety or structural-condition risk.

evidence.source_text: In states that do not have inspector licenses, inspectors that are professionally accredited members in good standing of a nationally recognized property inspection organization must be used.
In selected rural high-needs areas, Fannie Mae may oﬀer value acceptance through DU for certain transactions.

The rural high-needs value acceptance oﬀer will be considered for the following transactions only: loan caseﬁles that receive an Approve/Eligible recommendation; purchase transactions; one-unit principal residence properties (excluding manufactured homes); borrowers with income at or below 100% of the area median income; and LTV ratios up to 97% and CLTV ratios up to 105% with a Community Seconds.
These requirements must be met for the lender to exercise the rural high-needs value acceptance oﬀer.

business_rules.rule_name: Six-month lot-title condition for two-closing cash-out refinancing
business_rules.description: A permanent mortgage in a two-closing construction-to-permanent transaction may be closed as a cash-out refinance only when the borrower held legal title to the lot for at least six months before the permanent mortgage closing, subject to the applicable ratios and other standard cash-out requirements.

outcomes.value: property type provided in the Eligibility Matrix

business_rules.inference_reasoning: The source expressly limits the rule to two-closing construction-to-permanent transactions and identifies the permanent mortgage as the delivered loan.

source_reference.source_text: In a two-closing construction-to-permanent transaction, the permanent mortgage delivered to Fannie Mae may be closed as: a limited cash-out reﬁnance transaction, or a cash-out reﬁnance transaction. Two-closing construction-to-permanent mortgages are subject to the limited cash-out and cash-out reﬁnance maximum LTV, CLTV, and HCLTV ratios based on the property type provided in the Eligibility Matrix , as applicable. For the borrower to be eligible for a cash-out reﬁnance transaction, the borrower must have held legal title to the lot for at least six months prior to the closing of the permanent mortgage. All other standard cash-out reﬁnance eligibility and underwriting requirements apply. Note : Two-closing cash-out reﬁnances are not permitted on a manufactured home.

business_rules.rule_name: Two-closing construction-to-permanent transaction documentation and purchase treatment
business_rules.description: A two-closing construction-to-permanent mortgage uses separate closings and legal-document sets. The original note cannot be modified for the permanent financing; a new borrower-signed note is required. Fannie Mae does not purchase the interim construction loan but may purchase the permanent financing loan.
business_rules.inference_reasoning: The source expressly identifies two-closing construction-to-permanent mortgage transactions and distinguishes the interim construction financing from the permanent financing.

source_reference.source_text: Two-closing construction-to-permanent mortgage transactions utilize two separate loan closings with two separate sets of legal documents. A modiﬁcation may not be used to update the original note, rather a new note must be completed and signed by the borrower(s). The ﬁrst closing is to obtain the interim construction ﬁnancing (and may include the purchase of the lot), and the second closing is to obtain the permanent ﬁnancing upon completion of the improvements. Fannie Mae does not purchase construction loans (the ﬁrst closing); however, Fannie Mae does purchase loans that were used to provide the permanent ﬁnancing. The lender that provides the permanent long-term mortgage may be a diﬀerent lender than the one that provided the interim ﬁnancing. The lender must underwrite the borrower based on the terms of the permanent mortgage.

business_rules.rule_name: Appraise and Report Loans with Surviving Resale Restrictions
business_rules.description: For a loan secured by property with resale restrictions that survive foreclosure or a deed-in-lieu of foreclosure, the appraisal must reflect the restrictions' impact, use comparable sales with similar restrictions, and document the restrictions' effect on value and marketability. The lender must report SFC 631 at delivery.

source_reference.source_text: In cases where the resale restrictions survive foreclosure or a deed-in-lieu of foreclosure, the appraisal must reﬂect the impact the restrictions have on value and be supported by comparable sales with similar restrictions. The appraisal report must note the existence of the resale restrictions and comment on any impact the resale restrictions have on the property's value and marketability. Pricing and Delivery Considerations Pricing There are no speciﬁc LLPAs required for loans with resale restrictions. All other price adjustments that are otherwise applicable to the transaction will apply. For a list of current applicable LLPAs, see the Loan-Level Price Adjustment (LLPA) Matrix . Special Feature Codes Lenders must report SFC 631 when delivering a loan secured by a property with resale restrictions that survive foreclosure or a deed-in-lieu of foreclosure. No special feature code is required when delivering a loan secured by a property with resale restrictions that terminate automatically upon foreclosure (or the expiration of any applicable redemption period), or the recordation of a deed-in-lieu of foreclosure unless the loan is part of a shared equity transaction.

business_rules.rule_name: Limit Qualifying ADU Rental Income
business_rules.description: Rental income from an existing accessory dwelling unit may be used to qualify a borrower only for a one-unit principal residence, from no more than one ADU, in a purchase or limited cash-out refinance transaction, and the qualifying ADU rental income is limited to 30% of total qualifying income.
conditions: The property is a one-unit principal residence.
Rental income is derived from one existing ADU on the subject property.
The transaction is a purchase or limited cash-out refinance.
consequences: Qualifying rental income from the ADU must not exceed 30% of total qualifying income.
All other documentation and requirements in the rental income topic continue to apply.

business_rules.rule_name: Post-closing QC must request or reuse tax transcripts for underwriting income
business_rules.description: Post-closing quality control must validate income documentation used during underwriting by requesting transcripts for all income types used. When tax returns were required, the lender must reconcile IRS transcript information with income documents in the loan file.
business_rules.conditions: The loan is undergoing post-closing QC and the borrower's income was used during underwriting.
business_rules.consequences: The lender must request tax transcripts for all income types used in underwriting and reconcile transcript information with loan-file income documents when tax returns were required.
examples: A post-closing QC review requests transcripts for personal and business income used in underwriting.
A lender may reuse appropriate IRS transcripts obtained during preclosing underwriting.
business_rules.enforcement_action: Require income reverification or document the applicable transcript exception in the post-closing QC file.
business_rules.inference_reasoning: The cited passage expressly addresses post-closing QC, income used during underwriting, and the lender's transcript and reconciliation duties.

source_reference.source_text: Post-closing QC tax transcripts validate the income documentation provided by the borrower that was utilized during the underwriting process. Transcripts must be requested for all income types used in the underwriting process (personal and business, if applicable). If tax returns were required in the underwriting of the loan, the lender must reconcile the transcript information received from the IRS with the income documents in the loan ﬁle. See B3-3.1-02, Tax Return and Transcript Documentation Requirements , for detailed information. The following exception applies: If the lender obtained the appropriate IRS transcripts during its preclosing process (processing and underwriting), it may use the same documents in its post-closing QC process, without ordering new transcripts. The lender is not required to request tax transcripts for a borrower when all the borrower's income is validated by the DU validation service.

The two rules operate as complementary gates: acceptable property type and market acceptance are insufficient if the lease expires too soon.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If the lease-term extension is not verified, the loan may mature after the borrower's leasehold rights expire or become materially impaired. The lender may need a lease extension, amendment, or other cure, delaying closing or delivery.

business_rules.rule_name: Include Both Required MBS Disclosure Documents for Every Trade
business_rules.description: For any trade, whether TBA or otherwise, the lender's required disclosure must include both the applicable Single-Family Prospectus and the applicable Prospectus Supplement for the MBS program.
business_rules.inference_reasoning: The excerpt expressly states 'For any trade, TBA or otherwise' and identifies both required disclosure documents.

source_reference.source_text: The lender must provide the required disclosure documentation (described below) to a purchaser or prospective purchaser, as applicable. The lender will have two options to provide this disclosure: the lender must follow either the Standard Delivery option or the Alternative Website Delivery option, each as described below. The lender’s sale of securities—including any that Fannie Mae delivers based on the lender’s instructions on the Delivery Schedule (Form 2014 ) — also must comply with applicable securities disclosure and settlement requirements, including those set forth below under either the Standard Delivery option or the Alternative Website Delivery option. For any trade, TBA or otherwise, the required disclosure consists of both the Single-Family Prospectus and the Prospectus Supplement applicable to the MBS program.

business_rules.rule_name: Obtain a replacement appraisal when reliability concerns remain unresolved
business_rules.description: The lender must attempt to resolve concerns about the reliability of an appraisal's opinion of market value with the appraiser who prepared it. If the concerns cannot be resolved, the lender must obtain a replacement report before making the final underwriting decision.
consequences: A replacement appraisal report is obtained.
The replacement report is obtained before the final underwriting decision.

source_reference.source_text: The lender is responsible for conﬁrming that appraisal reports are complete and that any changes to the reports are made by the appraiser that originally completed the report. If the lender has concerns with any aspect of the appraisal that result in questions about the reliability of the opinion of market value, the lender must attempt to resolve its concerns with the appraiser that originally prepared the report. If the lender is unable to resolve its concerns with the appraiser, the lender must obtain a replacement report prior to making a ﬁnal underwriting decision on the loan. Any request for a change in the opinion of market value must be based on material and substantive issues and must not be made solely on the basis that the opinion of market value as indicated in the appraisal report does not support the proposed loan amount.

business_rules.rule_name: Submit the underwriting appraisal through UCDP and match the sale value
business_rules.description: When an appraisal report has subsequent revisions, the final version used for underwriting must be submitted through UCDP and receive a Successful status before sale to Fannie Mae. The submitted report must be unaltered, and the appraised value reported at sale must match the UCDP appraisal value, subject to the stated desk or field review exception.
consequences: The final appraisal version used for underwriting is submitted through UCDP.
UCDP returns a Successful status before sale to Fannie Mae.
The UCDP-submitted report is unaltered and was submitted by the identified appraiser.
The appraised value reported at sale matches the value on the appraisal submitted to UCDP.

source_reference.section_id: B4-1.2-01, Appraisal Report Forms and Exhibits (09/03/2025)
source_reference.source_text: there are subsequent revisions to the appraisal report, the ﬁnal version of the report that was utilized in making the underwriting decision must be submitted through the UCDP and receive a “Successful” status from the UCDP prior to sale of the loan to Fannie Mae. When submitting an appraisal report through the UCDP, lenders must ensure it is the unaltered report submitted by the identiﬁed appraiser. Additionally, for loans that require an appraisal, lenders must ensure the appraised value as indicated on the appraisal submitted to UCDP matches the appraised value as reported at sale of the loan. An exception is allowed for this requirement when the appraisal used to underwrite the loan is a desk or ﬁeld review of an existing appraisal because those types of reports cannot be submitted through the UCDP. In those instances, the appraised value reported at sale of the loan will reﬂect the value as stated in the desk or ﬁeld review.

source_reference.source_text: In addition to the limited waiver of underwriting representations and warranties available for certain DU loans, loans may also beneﬁt from enforcement relief of certain representations and warranties related to the appraisal and value of the subject property (without regard to underwriting method). business_rules.rule_name: Commitment Delivery Timing and Document Submission
business_rules.description: After receiving the applicable whole-loan or MBS commitment identifier and before commitment expiration, the lender must electronically submit loan data through Loan Delivery and send the documentation package to the document custodian.
business_rules.inference_reasoning: The source directly identifies whole-loan and MBS deliveries and specifies electronic Loan Delivery submission and document-custodian transmission.

source_reference.section_id: C1-2-01, General Information on Delivering Loan Data and Documents (05/01/2019) > Timing and Deadlines
source_reference.source_text: A lender can begin to deliver loans against its commitments as soon as it receives a commitment conﬁrmation number for whole loans, or an MBS commitment contract number for MBS loans. The lender must deliver the loans required to fulﬁll the commitment prior to the commitment expiration date. Speciﬁcally, lenders must submit loan data electronically, via Loan Delivery, and send the documentation package to the document custodian. Fannie Mae may reject a loan for a variety of reasons, including failure to meet Fannie Mae’s eligibility requirements, incomplete or inaccurate loan delivery data, or incomplete document submission packages. Fannie Mae may assess a late delivery fee for loans that are redelivered after a commitment has expired.

dependencies.rationale: B118 establishes the custodian relationship before an MBS commitment is obtained. B35 then requires delivery data submission and document transmission after the commitment identifier is received. Without the custody arrangement, the document package cannot be routed to an approved custodian.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: The lender cannot complete the MBS delivery setup, may miss the commitment expiration date, and may be unable to submit documents for certification. This can delay or prevent pool delivery and expose the lender to commitment fallout.

dependencies.rationale: B70 requires electronic UCD XML submission and a Successful status before delivery of a conventional loan. B35 is the delivery-stage rule for submitting the loan data and documentation package. The successful UCD result must be recorded before B35 permits delivery.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: Delivery must be blocked for a conventional loan without Successful UCD status. Proceeding without it can result in Fannie Mae rejection, repurchase exposure, and a compliance exception affecting the entire loan file.

dependencies.rationale: For a loan with subsequent appraisal revisions, the final underwriting appraisal must be submitted unaltered to UCDP and receive Successful status before sale to Fannie Mae. B35's delivery step must therefore check B29 before transmitting the loan for sale.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: Delivery or sale must be held until the final appraisal is successfully submitted and the reported value matches. Failure can lead to purchase rejection, valuation disputes, or repurchase risk.

dependencies.rationale: B38 is a direct pre-delivery gate. B35 must not submit the loan data or package for a project-unit loan until the lender has determined that the project satisfies Fannie Mae eligibility requirements.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: Delivery must be blocked. If the loan is delivered without project eligibility, Fannie Mae may reject or require repurchase of the loan, and the lender may incur significant borrower, investor, and operational remediation costs.

dependencies.rationale: B62 describes the appraisal-specific preparation and review sequence that must be completed before delivering a loan with a hybrid appraisal. B35 is the broader delivery execution step and should consume B62's outputs.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: Delivery may proceed with an incomplete or unreviewed appraisal, causing UCDP or investor rejection and requiring the loan to be withdrawn and corrected.

dependencies.rationale: B35 governs submission before commitment expiration. B24-002 imposes a transfer-agreement deadline tied to the delivery funding or MBS issuance event. The delivery workflow must therefore track agreement completion before the delivery reaches its funding or issuance endpoint.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: A loan may be delivered without a timely and enforceable servicing transfer, creating uncertainty over servicing responsibility and possible Fannie Mae approval or enforcement issues.

business_rules.rule_name: Calculate the Minimum Monthly Prefunding QC Sample
business_rules.description: Each month, the lender must select a prefunding QC sample using the lesser of 10% of the prior month's loans closed or acquired, 10% of the current month's projected loans to be closed or acquired, or 750 loans. The lender must also use a documented monthly process, account for origination risks and production channels, regularly review risk assessments, and include each production channel.

loan_types: loans closed or acquired subject to prefunding QC

business_rules.inference_reasoning: The excerpt expressly requires a monthly sample of loans closed or acquired and identifies production channels and origination risk as selection inputs; it does not state an occupancy limitation.

source_reference.source_text: The lender must establish and document a monthly process for selecting loans for its prefunding QC reviews. The process must take into account the lender’s assessment of the risks inherent in its origination processes, business sources, production channels, volume, and product mix. The lender must regularly review its risk assessments to ensure the sample selected is appropriate. The monthly sample must include selections from each of the lender's production channels. Each month, the lender must complete a minimum number of prefunding QC reviews. The monthly loan selection must equal, at a minimum, the lesser of: 10% of the prior month's total number of loans closed or acquired, or 10% of the current month's projected total number of loans to be closed or acquired (if using projections, the lender must perform a reconciliation process to ensure the 10% requirement is met); or 750 loans.

business_rules.rule_name: Maintain a Written Prefunding QC Plan
business_rules.description: A lender must maintain and implement a written prefunding quality control plan for reviewing a sample of loans before closing or, for loans acquired from a delegated third party, before acquisition. The plan must document timing, loan selection, and verification of data and documents.

loan_types: mortgage loans reviewed under lender prefunding QC

business_rules.inference_reasoning: The excerpt expressly limits the review timing to before closing or before acquisition and does not identify an occupancy-type limitation.

source_reference.source_text: The lender must maintain and implement a written prefunding QC plan that outlines requirements for reviewing a sample of its loans prior to closing or, in the case of loans acquired from a delegated third party, prior to acquisition. The lender must have documented procedures that include, at a minimum, the following elements: timing of the prefunding QC ﬁle reviews, loan selection process, and veriﬁcation of data and documents. The lender’s prefunding QC process must operate independent of the lender’s production process, if practical. At a minimum, prefunding QC must be conducted by individuals who have no involvement in the origination, processing or underwriting functions of the loan being reviewed.

business_rules.rule_name: eNote MERS eRegistry Registration Timing and Controller
business_rules.description: Lenders must maintain process controls to register eNotes in the MERS eRegistry as soon as possible after the tamper-evident seal is applied and no later than one business day after signing. The originating lender must be the first Controller, and subsequent changes of Control must be reflected in the registry.
business_rules.conditions: An eNote has been signed and its tamper-evident seal has been applied.
business_rules.consequences: The eNote is registered in the MERS eRegistry within the required period with the originating lender as first Controller; subsequent transfers are recorded.

outcomes.value: no later than one business day after signing

business_rules.inference_reasoning: The source expressly addresses lenders registering eNotes in the MERS eRegistry and states the timing, initial Controller, assumed-name treatment, and subsequent transfer requirements.

source_reference.section_id: B8-8-02, Requirements for Creating, Closing, and Correcting eNotes (12/13/2023) - Requirements for Registering eNotes
source_reference.source_text: Lenders must have process controls in place to ensure eNotes are registered in the MERS eRegistry as soon as possible after the tamper-evident seal has been applied, but no later than one business day after signing. The record in the MERS eRegistry must reﬂect the originating lender - the lender whose name is on the eNote - as the ﬁrst Controller. The following applies to lenders using tradenames or assumed names on eNotes: the legal entity name must also be included on the eNote (for example, ABC Financial, Inc., dba XYZ Mortgage); and the initial MERS eRegistry registration must reﬂect the legal entity name as the initial Controller. Any and all subsequent transfers of the eNotes - changes of Control - must be reﬂected in the MERS eRegistry.

business_rules.rule_name: Completion Documentation Must Contain Verifiable Exhibits
business_rules.description: Completion documentation using Form 1004D or an alternative method must include visually verifiable exhibits. When digital exhibits are linked from the form, the link must remain accessible to Fannie Mae for the life of the loan, and the exhibits must be unaltered and authenticatable using metadata and the subject property's geocode.

source_reference.section_id: B4-1.2-05, Requirements for Verifying Completion and Postponed Improvements (12/10/2025)
source_reference.source_text: The Appraisal Update and/or Completion Report (Form 1004D ) is used to update an appraisal or provide conﬁrmation that the requirements or conditions in an appraisal report have been met (such as completion of construction or repairs). The appraiser can complete the Completion Report section of Form 1004D based on an on-site visual inspection of the property. The appraiser may also complete the form based on alternative methods, such as virtual inspections, digital photos, site videos, or other technological solutions. All completion documentation must include one or more visually veriﬁable exhibits. A link to the digital exhibits from within the form is acceptable but must be accessible by Fannie Mae for the life of the loan. These exhibits must be unaltered and able to be authenticated using metadata and the geocode for the subject property.

business_rules.rule_name: Cash-Out Refinance Eligibility for Manufactured Homes
business_rules.description: A cash-out refinance secured by a manufactured home is eligible only when the property is a multi-width manufactured home, the borrower has owned both the manufactured home and land for at least 12 months before the loan application date, and the LTV, CLTV, and HCLTV ratios are based on the current appraised value of the manufactured home and land.

consequences.value: current appraised value of manufactured home and land

outcomes.value: current appraised value of manufactured home and land

business_rules.enforcement_action: A single-width manufactured home is not eligible for this cash-out refinance transaction.
business_rules.inference_reasoning: The cited passage expressly states the conditions for a cash-out refinance to be eligible and identifies the manufactured-home transaction scope.

source_reference.source_text: Reﬁnance Transactions A cash-out reﬁnance: involves the payoﬀ of an existing ﬁrst lien mortgage secured by the manufactured home and land (or existing liens if the home and land were encumbered by separate ﬁrst liens); or enables the property owner to obtain a mortgage on a property that does not already have a mortgage lien against it, and permits the borrower to take equity out of the property in the form of mortgage proceeds that may be used for any purpose. To be eligible for a cash-out reﬁnance, the property must be a multi-width manufactured home (single-width are not permitted). The borrower must have owned both the manufactured home and land for at least 12 months preceding the date of the loan application. The LTV, CLTV, and HCLTV ratios will be based on the current appraised value of the manufactured home and land.

business_rules.rule_name: High LTV refinance appraisal representation relief
business_rules.description: For a High LTV Refinance where the lender obtains an appraisal, the lender is relieved from standard representations and warranties concerning property marketability and condition as reflected in the valuation, but remains responsible for the appraisal as it relates to value. Properties rated C6 and/or Q6 may be delivered on an as-is basis without requiring the appraisal to be completed subject to repairs.
business_rules.inference_reasoning: The source expressly introduces the rule under 'For all High LTV Reﬁnances' and conditions it on obtaining an appraisal.

source_reference.section_id: B5-7-04, High LTV Refinance Representations and Warranties (03/01/2023)
source_reference.source_text: For all High LTV Reﬁnances If the lender obtains an appraisal for the subject property, the lender is not responsible for the standard representations and warranties related to the marketability and condition of the property as reﬂected in the property valuation. The lender remains responsible for the appraisal as it pertains to the value. Lenders may deliver loans on properties with a condition rating of C6 and/or a quality rating of Q6 completed on an “as-is” basis. There is no requirement for the appraisal to be completed “subject to” repairs being made.

examples: Lenders sell or deliver mortgage loans to Fannie Mae.

dependencies.rationale: B76-R004 requires uninsured damage or damage affecting safety, soundness, or structural integrity to be repaired before delivery to Fannie Mae. B80-R05 requires the loan to be eligible for purchase before proceeds can be wired. Therefore, the repair outcome is a prerequisite to the eligibility condition used by the proceeds rule. This dependency does not apply when the B76 high-LTV refinance exception applies.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If required repairs are incomplete, the lender must block delivery, place the loan on hold, or cure the property defect. Proceeding could make the loan ineligible for purchase, delay funding, and expose the lender to repurchase or indemnification risk.

dependencies.rationale: B91-R04 requires the lender to specify a valid and appropriate payee code and complete the related Form 482 and delivery-update steps. B80-R05 expressly requires a valid designated payee code before whole-loan sale proceeds are wired. The source rule therefore supplies a direct, mandatory input to the target rule.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If the payee code or related designation process fails, Fannie Mae cannot route proceeds to the intended account. Funding may be delayed, the loan may require delivery correction, and operational or fraud-control exceptions may be triggered.

dependencies.rationale: B93 prohibits delivery under Conditional Project Approval, Ineligible, or Suspension of the Application designations and requires a valid Fannie Mae Final Project Approval before delivery. B80 requires the loan to be eligible for purchase. The final project approval result is therefore a direct eligibility prerequisite for proceeds.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If final approval is absent or the project has a prohibited designation, the loan must not be delivered or funded through the purchase process. Incorrect delivery may create an immediate eligibility defect and potential repurchase liability.

dependencies.rationale: B99 requires applicable delivery data and income information to be reported at delivery for every high-LTV refinance loan, including transactions without a maximum DTI ratio. B80 requires accurate loan delivery data by the applicable cutoff time before proceeds are wired. B99 therefore supplies a conditional delivery-data gate.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: Missing or inaccurate high-LTV refinance reporting can prevent the custodian from accepting the package or cause the loan to fail delivery-data validation. This may delay proceeds and create a post-delivery data defect.

dependencies.rationale: For properties with resale restrictions surviving foreclosure or deed-in-lieu, B108 requires the appraisal to reflect the restrictions and their effect on value and marketability and requires SFC 631 at delivery. B80 requires a complete and accurate mortgage document package and delivery data. B108 is therefore a specialized package-completeness and accuracy control.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: Failure can cause delivery-data or document-package rejection, inaccurate collateral valuation, and possible purchase eligibility or repurchase concerns. The lender may need a corrected appraisal or corrected delivery data before proceeds can be released.

dependencies.rationale: B122 prohibits delivery immediately after receipt of Fannie Mae's notice when the property was appraised by the identified appraiser. B80 permits proceeds only when the loan is eligible for purchase. A prohibited delivery cannot satisfy the purchase-eligibility condition, so the notice and appraiser-status check must occur before funding.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If the lender ignores the notice, the loan may be delivered in violation of an immediate prohibition. Delivery and proceeds must be stopped, and the lender may need a new appraisal or other approved remediation.

dependencies.rationale: When employment or self-employment income is used to qualify, B27 requires a timely VOE, an allowable alternative, or an authorized post-closing VOE obtained no later than delivery. If none is available before delivery, the loan is ineligible for sale. B80 requires purchase eligibility before sending proceeds, making B27 a direct eligibility prerequisite.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: The lender must stop sale and proceeds processing, obtain the VOE or allowable alternative if still permissible, or remove the loan from the sale. Delivery without the required evidence creates a clear sale-eligibility defect and potential repurchase exposure.

dependencies.rationale: RULE-114 requires SFC 176 when a loan with shared appreciation is delivered. B80 requires accurate loan delivery data before proceeds are sent. The source is a specialized delivery-data control that must be satisfied in addition to the generic proceeds conditions.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If SFC 176 is omitted, delivery data may be inaccurate or rejected, delaying purchase proceeds and potentially creating a loan-delivery defect.

dependencies.rationale: B118-R002 requires SFC 009 when the loan has a moderate interest rate buydown. B80 requires accurate loan delivery data before wiring sale proceeds. The special-feature-code rule therefore supplies a conditional data element to the target process.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: Omission or miscoding can cause delivery-data rejection, delay funding, and require correction before the loan is treated as eligible for purchase proceeds.

dependencies.rationale: B118-R003 requires SFC 014 for a significant interest rate buydown. B80 requires accurate loan delivery data before proceeds are wired. The source rule therefore provides a specialized conditional data requirement that complements the generic delivery process.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If SFC 014 is missing or incorrect, the delivery record may fail validation, delaying purchase proceeds and requiring correction or escalation.

dependencies.rationale: B109 identifies when a best-efforts commitment can be fulfilled through a valid DU Approve/Eligible recommendation or the Other Underwriting Method. B80 requires the loan to be eligible for purchase before proceeds are sent. B109 is therefore one important underwriting and commitment-eligibility component of the broader purchase decision.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If the best-efforts commitment cannot be fulfilled, the loan may not qualify for the intended sale execution. Proceeds may be withheld, the loan may require a different execution, or the lender may incur fallout and repricing risk.

dependencies.rationale: B67 requires eligible gross monthly rent to be reported in Fannie Mae loan delivery data. B80 conditions wire transfer of whole-loan sale proceeds on the custodian receiving complete and accurate loan delivery data by the applicable cutoff. When both rules apply to the same loan, completion of B67 is a data prerequisite to the delivery condition in B80.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If the rent is not reported, delivery data may be incomplete or inaccurate, causing the loan to miss the cutoff, delaying purchase proceeds, generating delivery corrections, or preventing the loan from being purchased until the data is corrected.

business_rules.rule_name: Repurchase for Untimely Government Guaranty or Insurance
business_rules.description: After delivery of a mortgage loan, if the lender fails to obtain the government guaranty or insurance in a timely manner as determined by Fannie Mae, the lender must repurchase the mortgage and make Fannie Mae whole for losses incurred. Fannie Mae may also suspend or terminate the lender's authority to deliver specified government mortgages or any mortgage.
business_rules.conditions: The mortgage loan has been delivered and the lender fails to obtain the required government guaranty or insurance in a timely manner as determined by Fannie Mae.
business_rules.inference_reasoning: The cited text expressly applies after delivery of a mortgage loan and identifies failure to obtain government guaranty or insurance as the triggering event.

source_reference.source_text: After delivery of a mortgage loan, if a lender fails to obtain the guaranty or insurance in a timely manner, as determined by Fannie Mae, the lender must repurchase the mortgage and make Fannie Mae whole for any losses incurred by Fannie Mae. In addition, Fannie Mae may suspend or terminate the lender’s authority to deliver the following: mortgages for which it has not already received the government mortgage guaranty or insurance, any government mortgage or any particular category of government mortgage, or any mortgage.

business_rules.description: A project qualifies as a PUD only when unit-owner HOA membership is automatic and nonseverable, unit assessments are mandatory, common property and improvements are owned and maintained by an HOA for unit-owner benefit and use, and the subject unit is not legally created as part of a condo or co-op project.

The subject unit is not legally created as part of a condo or co-op project.

loan_types: mortgage loans secured by units in PUD projects

business_rules.rule_name: Unemployment Benefits Income History and Qualifying Income
business_rules.description: Unemployment benefits income may be considered when qualifying the borrower when the required two-year history and tax-return documentation are present. The lender calculates qualifying income using the most recent two years for stable or increasing income and the most recent year for decreasing income. Continuance need not be verified unless there is reason to believe the income may not continue.
conditions: The income type is unemployment benefits.
At least two years of income history are present.
Two years of signed personal federal income tax returns are obtained.
The historical income trend is stable or increasing, or decreasing.
The lender has no reason to believe the income may not continue.
consequences: The unemployment benefits income may be considered for qualifying.
For stable or increasing income, qualifying income is averaged using the most recent two years of personal federal income tax returns.
For decreasing income, qualifying income is averaged using the most recent year of personal federal income tax returns.
Continuance verification is not required under the stated no-reason-to-doubt condition.

examples.scenario: Unemployment benefits have a two-year history supported by two years of signed personal federal income tax returns and the income is stable or increasing.
examples.result: Average the most recent two years.

examples.scenario: Unemployment benefits have a two-year history supported by two years of signed personal federal income tax returns and the income is decreasing.

business_rules.enforcement_action: Do not use the unemployment benefits income for qualifying unless the minimum history and documentation requirements are met; apply the stated trend-based calculation.

business_rules.rule_name: Form 520 Submission and Signature Requirements
business_rules.description: A seller/servicer must deliver five executed original Form 520 documents to Fannie Mae, with all signatures provided through traditional in-person ink-signed methods and without remote notarization or eNotarization, unless the seller/servicer qualifies as a housing finance agency and receives Fannie Mae verification of that status.

source_reference.section_id: A4-1-04, Submission of Irrevocable Limited Powers of Attorney (05/04/2022)
source_reference.source_text: Seller/servicers must complete and deliver ﬁve executed original Form 520 to Fannie Mae at the address indicated on the instructions to the form. See below for an exception to this requirement. All signatures on the Form 520 must be provided using traditional in-person ink-signed methods. Irrespective of the law of the place of execution, the notary may not use the remote in-person method of signatory authentication and signature witnessing or eNotarization, including remote online notarization, to satisfy the notarization of the Form 520 . The Form 520 does not modify the duties and obligations of the parties under the Lender Contract. The Form 520 is a free-standing remedial instrument intended to preserve and protect Fannie Mae's interest in loans serviced by the seller/servicer. In the event of exigent circumstances, Fannie Mae will use the power of attorney at its sole discretion (for example, when for whatever reason a seller/servicer is unable or unwilling to execute Published March 4, 2026 147requested assignments of mortgages on a timely basis). In lieu of the Form 520, a seller/servicer that is a housing ﬁnance agency, as deﬁned in 24 C.F.R. §266.5, may submit a letter conﬁrming that it meets such deﬁnition. After Fannie Mae has reviewed and veriﬁed compliance with the deﬁnition, the seller/servicer will be exempt from this requirement.

business_rules.description: Income used to qualify a borrower must have a stable and predictable flow, a documented history of receipt, and a reasonable expectation of continuance; the lender must evaluate continuance based on the income's nature and supporting documentation.

dependencies.rationale: BR-111-BORROWER-001 establishes the general standard that qualifying income must have a documented receipt history and reasonable continuance. RULE-100 provides the more specific treatment for public assistance income and modifies the history requirement. The specific rule should be evaluated first when public assistance is the income source, after which the general stability and continuance assessment remains applicable.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If RULE-100 is not satisfied, public assistance income cannot be treated as qualifying income under the special zero-month-history treatment. The lender must either obtain the missing agency documentation, payment evidence, or continuance evidence, or exclude the income from qualification. Applying the general rule without the specific exception could result in an incorrect income-history requirement.

dependencies.rationale: When foreign income is used to qualify, B102 establishes that the lender has compliant documentation for the income source. BR-111-BORROWER-001 then evaluates whether that documented income is stable, historically received, and reasonably expected to continue. The foreign-income documentation is therefore an evidentiary input to the broader income-eligibility assessment.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If B102 fails, the lender cannot reliably evaluate the foreign income under BR-111. The income must be excluded or the missing tax returns, translations, currency conversion, or source documentation must be obtained. Proceeding without this validation creates a risk of overstated qualifying income and inaccurate underwriting.

dependencies.rationale: BR-111 requires the lender to evaluate the stability and expected continuance of qualifying income. B117-R01 specifies the acceptable verification evidence for military income and substitutes that evidence for an ordinary VOE. The military verification result should therefore be available before the lender completes the general qualifying-income assessment.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If military income verification is unavailable or stale, the lender cannot complete a reliable stability and continuance review for that income. The file may be suspended, the income excluded, or a compliant LES or DMDC verification requested. Using an ordinary VOE instead of the permitted military evidence could create a documentation defect.

dependencies.rationale: For self-employed income, BR-111 requires the lender to assess stable and predictable income with a reasonable expectation of continuance. B117-R02 supplies a current business-existence check and a documented verification source. That evidence helps validate the business-related income source before the general income conclusion is finalized.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If the business cannot be verified within the 120-day window, the lender may be unable to establish that the self-employment income source remains active. The income may be excluded, the underwriting decision suspended, or updated third-party verification required.

dependencies.rationale: B121 supplies signed federal tax returns and the applicable reporting periods and forms. Those records support the history-of-receipt and income-trend portions of BR-111. The lender must still evaluate whether the income is stable and reasonably expected to continue, including consideration of current business verification and other documentation.
dependencies.impact_if_fails: If the required tax returns are not obtained or are incomplete, the lender may not be able to substantiate the borrower's income history. The self-employed income calculation may be suspended, reduced, or excluded, delaying underwriting and potentially changing the borrower's debt-to-income ratio.

business_rules.rule_name: Use Earned Real Estate Commission as Eligible Funds
business_rules.description: A lender may use a borrower's earned real estate commission as an eligible source of funds for down payment and closing costs when the borrower is acting as their own real estate agent, is licensed, and will receive a sales commission from purchasing the subject property. The lender must document the settlement statement treatment and credit the commission toward the mortgage loan.

The borrower is a licensed real estate agent.
The borrower will receive a sales commission from the purchase of the subject property.
consequences: The earned real estate commission may be used as an eligible source of funds for down payment and closing costs.
The settlement statement must reflect the commission earned by the borrower.
The earned commission amount must be credited toward the mortgage loan.

source_reference.section_id: B3-4.3-21, Borrower's Earned Real Estate Commission (04/05/2023)
source_reference.source_text: Earned real estate commission refers to the borrower's portion of a real estate commission earned from the sale of the subject property being purchased when the borrower is acting as their own real estate agent. Lenders may use the borrower's earned real estate commission as an eligible source of funds for down payment and closing costs provided the borrower is a licensed real estate agent and will receive a sales commission from the purchase of the subject property. Documentation Requirements The lender must document the following: the settlement statement must reﬂect the commission earned by the borrower, and the earned commission amount must be credited towards the mortgage loan.

business_rules.rule_name: Correction of significant defects during appeal or impasse
business_rules.description: For a mortgage loan with a significant defect, Fannie Mae requires repurchase or may offer a repurchase alternative. During appeal or impasse, the lender may provide a correction within the time frame and manner required by the Lender Contract, and additional documentation or information receives the same quality-control review standard as the initial mortgage file documentation.

loan_types: mortgage loans covered by the remedies framework

business_rules.inference_reasoning: The source expressly identifies significant defects and the appeal and impasse processes, and directly states the lender’s correction right and review standard.

source_reference.section_id: Overview of Process — Step 2—Correcting Certain Signiﬁcant Defects
source_reference.source_text: If Fannie Mae identiﬁes a signiﬁcant defect, Fannie Mae will require repurchase of the mortgage loan or may oﬀer the lender a repurchase alternative. Step 2—Correcting Certain Signiﬁcant Defects During the appeal and impasse processes, a lender has the right to provide a correction of any signiﬁcant defect in the speciﬁed time frame and in the manner required by the Lender Contract. Any additional documentation or information that the lender provides is subject to the same standard of quality control review as the initial mortgage ﬁle documentation.
